<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **7** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **55** of **207** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **19** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 8222fa805d0e288fec470e47e374e408b4925745` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `c4294495678b00d7410f4dc0c33b10f21857e3c5`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/objectql/src/engine.ts, packages/objectql/src/summary-batch-accumulation.ts, packages/objectql/src/summary-batch-accumulation.test.ts, packages/rest/src/import-batch-parent-summary-rule.test.ts + packages/objectql/src/engine-master-detail-related.ts (the one-hop loader behind `resolvePredicateRelated`: projection, `id`, null materialisation), packages/objectql/src/having-filter.ts (`matchesAggregationFilter`, `declaredFieldClasses`, `declaredJsonStoredFields`), packages/objectql/src/summary-aggregate.ts (`SummaryDescriptor`, `summaryEmptySetValue`), packages/objectql/src/validation/rule-validator.ts (`RelatedRecordBinding`), packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-batch-data.ts (`createManyData`, `insertManyData`), packages/core/src/utils/import-runner.ts (the create flush, `previewVerdict`), apps/docs/lib/i18n.ts, skills/objectstack-data/rules/relationships.md, docs/adr/0087-metadata-protocol-upgrade-contract.md; prose faces read for ②: .changeset/25579-batch-parent-summary-rule.md, content/docs/data-modeling/fields.mdx

Face: narrowing — `record-recognisers --template --paths` on the six changed paths answers that the paths decide no face and the changeset's `Clause-②:` line decides; it carries the `(narrowing)` arm, so `--face narrowing`. The floor is the four code/test paths; no path is a remainder.

Read at 2026-10-27T12:51Z: card #25579 body and all 3 comments (re-lane `6438806805`, claim `6440245607`, os-dev-report `6442152067`), PR #26680 body and file list (6 files, +625/-2), `git diff origin/main...c4294495678b00d7410f4dc0c33b10f21857e3c5` (merge-base `a76f811e0e`; the head is the merge of `origin/main` `8222fa805d` into 4 branch commits), cited code at the head via `git show`, and the 44 check-runs on the head.

### ① Derived judgments

**D1 — the narrowing, named per door (right).** On `main` a bulk insert resolved the related rows its predicate rules read ONE time for the whole batch (`resolvePredicateRelated`, engine.ts 15727) and recomputed the parent summary ONE time after the driver write (16004). At the head, `insert()` builds `createBatchSummaryAccumulator(this.getSummaryDescriptors(object), fields)` when the batch holds more than one row (the `rows.length` gate, 15734–15736), overlays it on each row's `related` binding in the validation loop (15756), and calls `accept(rows[i])` only after `evaluateValidationRules` AND `assertReferencesResolve` returned (15757–15761). So the requests that were accepted on `main` and are refused at the head are exactly: a multi-row create in which a later row's rule reads a parent `summary` one hop through `related`, where the earlier rows of the same call that the rules admitted move that summary past the rule's limit. The doors, read in the cited code:
- `engine.insert(object, array)` — the accumulator's seat; refuses the whole batch (non-partial mode rethrows at 15763). Pinned by the rest test's "insert(array) all or nothing".
- `engine.insertMany` — `this.insert(object, rows, { __partialRowErrors: true })` (16122–16125); the refused row gets `rowErrors[i]` and the rest land. Pinned.
- `createManyData` — protocol-batch-data.ts: `this.engine.insert(request.object, request.records, opts)`, so it is `insert(array)`.
- `insertManyData` — protocol-batch-data.ts: `this.engine.insertMany(...)`.
- the import commit — import-runner.ts flushes buffered creates through `insertManyData` when the protocol has it (`writeBatchPartial`, 1110), else `createManyData` (`writeBatch`); chunked at `Math.min(progressEvery, MAX_CREATE_BATCH_SIZE)` (1094). A file larger than one chunk is several engine calls, and between calls the recompute has written the stored value the next call's hop reads, so 批量等于逐条 holds across chunks too. Pinned end to end by the rest test's acceptance case through `POST /api/v1/data/:object/import`.
- the multi-row `validate` preview — insert mode and more than one row (the `mode` and `rows.length` gate, 14672–14674), overlay at 14729, `accept(row)` at 14738 after a `ValidationError` has already returned `valid: false` (14731–14737). Pinned ("answers what the write answers, and writes nothing").

**D2 — unchanged, confirmed in the code (right).** Single-row writes: the accumulator is `undefined` for `rows.length === 1` and `validate` in insert mode with one row, so the binding passes through untouched; pinned ("a single write behaves as before"). Bulk updates: both `resolvePredicateRelated` calls in `update()` (the by-id `updateView` at 17498, the predicate `bulkRelatedForRow` at 17840) are untouched by the diff and no accumulator exists there; `validate` in update mode is gated out by `mode === 'insert'`. Each door's success semantics: `insertMany` still culls per row, `insert(array)` still throws, the recompute at 16004 still runs once over the written rows. Nothing is widened: `overlay` only ever moves a summary value upward for `count`/`sum` and toward the admitted extreme for `min`/`max`, and a value it cannot say exactly is left stored, so no row that `main` refused is admitted at the head.

**D3 — ruling 6377847361 letter C, per-row re-read forbidden (right).** `summary-batch-accumulation.ts` imports no engine, driver or registry (lines 51–54: a descriptor type, `summaryEmptySetValue`, the having-filter walker, the binding types). `accept` reads only `row`; `overlay` reads only the binding the already-batched hop produced and returns copies (`patched ??= { ...related }`, `out ??= { ...binding }`, 183–188; pinned "the shared row is never mutated"). The accumulator is built once per call, after the one pre-existing batched read. ⛔ No database read was added. A refused row is never counted: in `insert()` `accept` sits last inside the same `try` as the rules and the reference check, so a throw skips it; rows dead from the earlier per-row loops (`rowErrors[i] !== undefined`, 15745) never reach it; in `validate()` the `ValidationError` branch returns before `accept`. Pinned by "a row the rules refuse does not raise the count a later row reads" (rest) and "a row never accepted moves nothing" (objectql).

**D4 — a row admitted but failed by a later step of the same write (right, and the dev's note is accurate).** After the validation loop, under `partialMode` the autonumber issue loop (15811–15823) can set `rowErrors[i]` for a row `accept` already counted; that row lands nowhere while a later row of the batch read it in the overlay, so the later row can be refused where one-by-one writes would admit it. The driver write (`bulkCreate`, 15867–15895) does not degrade per row at this layer: a failure there throws `envelopeDriverWriteRefusal` for the whole live batch, so no row lands and the question does not arise. The window is one step wide, is a fault (not a rule verdict), and errs only in the refusing direction. The Acceptance notes say exactly this. Judged acceptable; see ③-F2.

**D5 — which summary kinds accumulate exactly (right).** `ACCUMULABLE = {count, sum, min, max}` (76); `avg` and any descriptor whose `filter` names a dotted path are dropped at construction (109, `filterNamesDottedPath` walks `$and`/`$or`/`$not`); a descriptor that meets a non-finite or non-number `sourceField` value, or whose filter the walker refuses, is added to `dropped` and reads the stored value for the rest of the batch (129, 138) — sticky for every parent, which is the conservative side. A stored value that is not a number is left as it is (`moved` returns `undefined`, 157). `null` on the row is skipped as SQL does (137); a stored `null` starts at `summaryEmptySetValue(fn)` (156), the same seed `initializeSummaryFields` and the recompute use. The filter is evaluated on the new row with the child's declared field classes and JSON-stored set, the recompute's own walker. All eleven objectql cases pin these. The docs page (`fields.mdx` +312–+328) states the batch rule, the four exact kinds, the three kept-as-stored cases, 批量等于逐条 and 并发不保证, in the words the ruling asks for; the changeset's "Which summaries accumulate" bullet says the same. The docs site is `languages: ['en']` (apps/docs/lib/i18n.ts:14), so no translation is owed. `skills/objectstack-data/rules/relationships.md` "Roll-up Summaries" (189–215) states only that the engine recomputes server-side on child writes and the empty-set values; nothing there becomes false.

**D6 — the binding the overlay keys on (right).** `overlay` requires `related.id` (173) and `desc.summaryField in related` (178). The one-hop loader's projection always names `id` alongside the fields the rules read (engine.ts 10184–10188) and materialises a declared column the driver omitted to `null` (engine-master-detail-related.ts 476), so the key is present exactly when a rule reads the roll-up, and a `null` there is the never-computed base. A binding that is `unavailable`, names another parent object, or names a parent no admitted row moved passes through by identity (pinned).

**D7 — public surface (right).** No change to `packages/objectql/src/index.ts`, `packages/metadata-protocol/**`, `packages/spec/**` or `docs/adr/**` (diff-stat on those paths is empty). `createBatchSummaryAccumulator` is a module-internal export used by `engine.ts` only. The protocol doors' request and response shapes are untouched. `Metadata-protocol: none` is right.

**D8 — the dogfood battery (right).** The PR body's "Dogfood battery (narrowing arm)" block and the os-dev-report's `dogfood_battery` field agree: on `c429449567`, `pnpm --filter @objectstack/dogfood test` under the verify lock, no shard, after a full build: Test Files 301 passed | 3 skipped (304), Tests 2501 passed | 18 skipped (2519), `os-verify-lock: VERDICT command-exit 0`, held 1286s. `c429449567` is this head. Full (no shard), no failures; the skips are declared skips, not reds. review-checklist.md :50 is met.

**D9 — check-runs on the head, read at 2026-10-27T12:51Z (44).** Completed `success` (14): Auto Label, Check Changeset, Check Documentation Links, Check PR Size, Dogfood Regression Gate, Flag docs affected by code changes, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Lint · PM dispatch-gates, Lint · scoped · tooling self-tests, PR-body guards, Plan Test Core shards, Spec property liveness, Test UI, filter. Completed `skipped` (10, the UI, opt-in, temporal and sharded twins the job-level gates skip on this diff): 18.x upgrade harness, Build & E2E UI, Build UI Deps, Dogfood Regression Gate shards, Dogfood Verify CLI, Lint UI, Packed-tarball smoke, Temporal Conformance, Test UI shards, Type Check UI. Still `in_progress` (20): Build Core, Build Docs, Lint · CI release & engine gates, Lint · ESLint, Lint · docs & code guards, Lint · repo & tooling gates, Lint · scoped · query-options erasure, Lint · scoped · slot lookup & corpus, Test Core 1/8 through 8/8, Type Check · consumer gates, Type Check · debt ledger, Type Check · source gates, Type Check · workspace. No failure at read time. The derived gate families (Test Core, Type Check, the Lint set) have not concluded; their conclusions are the gate verdicts, so the queue entry waits on them (checklist: 入队另要求全 check 绿). This record judges the contract, not those runs.

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/25579-batch-parent-summary-rule.md`: `'@objectstack/objectql': patch`, title `fix(objectql)!:`, a **BREAKING** block that names the narrowing, who sees it and the remedy, both declaration lines, and the ADR-0087 comment `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`.

- **Level.** `patch` with the BREAKING block is right for what the diff publishes: no export, type, schema key or protocol shape moves (D7); an already-declared validation rule is now enforced inside one bulk create as it is enforced one write at a time; the refusal is the rule's own `VALIDATION_FAILED`. The published change is an accept-set narrowing of the bulk insert, and the body says so. Only `@objectstack/objectql` is named, and only objectql source changed (the rest and core packages carry a test and nothing else); `Check Changeset` is `success`.
- **Clause-②: no (narrowing)** — matches D1/D2 on the measured diff: a batch row admitted before can be refused, nothing is admitted that was refused. Same line on the PR body and the changeset.
- **Metadata-protocol: none** — right (D7).
- **ADR-0087 `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`** — right: no key of any schema is added, removed, renamed or re-shaped, the body carries no FROM/TO arrow or framed table (its "Before / Now" are prose bullets on runtime behaviour), so the disposition is admitted and nothing is prescribed to migrate.
- **Skills-docs: none** — right (D5, relationships.md).

### ③ Boundary flags

`open_questions: []` — none to answer. Dev flags, from the PR's Acceptance notes and the os-dev-report's `out_of_scope_findings`:

- **F1 — import dry run diverges from the commit** (class a, reported to the seat). Confirmed: `previewVerdict` (import-runner.ts 963–979) sends `data` as one row per `validateData` call, so a dry run of the card's two rows reads the stored summary for each and answers both valid, while the commit flush creates one and refuses the other. Not a narrowing of any write (the dry run writes nothing) and not the card's acceptance (the ruling's acceptance is the commit: 「两行只建成一行，另一行报规则错误」). The engine's multi-row preview does accumulate (D1), so the fix is a one-call change in `import-runner.ts` to preview the buffered creates as one multi-row `validateData`. Escalated to the seat as a follow-up card; not a blocker here.
- **F2 — partial mode, a row admitted then failed by a later step is still counted.** Answered in D4: the step is the autonumber issue under `insertMany`; the direction is refuse-only; a fault, not a rule verdict. Acceptable as documented in the PR body. Not owed on the docs page: the ruling's documented limit is concurrency, and this is not a limit of the rule's meaning.
- **F3 — the `parent` root of a master-detail `requiredWhen` is not accumulated.** Confirmed: `insertParentForRow` (15721–15723, gated on `hasParentScopedRequiredWhen`) is resolved once per batch and no overlay touches it. The card's rule reads through `related` (a `lookup`), which is what the ruling's acceptance exercises. Outside the card; escalated to the seat as a candidate follow-up (a `requiredWhen` that reads a parent summary through `master_detail` keeps the pre-fix batch reading).
- **F4 — bulk updates not covered.** Confirmed unchanged (D2). The card is titled on the bulk insert and the ruling's acceptance is the import's create; the seat's own question asks to confirm bulk updates unchanged. Outside the card; noted, not filed.
- **F5 — concurrency.** Out of scope by the ruling and stated on the docs page and in the changeset (并发不保证). Answered.
- **F6 — reviewer's own flag, the preview's accept point.** `validate()` calls `accept(row)` after the rules alone (14738); `insert()` calls it after the rules AND `assertReferencesResolve` (15758–15761). A preview row whose reference on a field no rule traverses dangles is counted in the preview and refused by the write, so a multi-row preview can refuse a later row the write admits. Refuse-only, one step wide, same family as F1 (preview/commit divergence). Not a narrowing of a write; noted for the F1 follow-up, not a blocker.
